questions.q:
Name the validation check used in each case:
(a) a date must be entered in the form DD/MM/YYYY [1]
(b) the number of tickets must be an integer, not text. [1]
A program accepts whole numbers from 1 to 20 inclusive. Give the boundary test data for this range.
questions.model: Lower boundary: 1 should be accepted and 0 rejected. Upper boundary: 20 should be accepted and 21 rejected.
questions.tip: Boundary data = the largest/smallest accepted value AND the value just outside it.

questions.q: Show the list 8, 3, 5, 1 after each pass of a bubble sort into ascending order, and state how the algorithm knows the list is sorted.
ms: a pass is made with no swaps (a flag stays FALSE) so the algorithm stops / allow: after n − 1 passes (1)
questions.model:
Pass 1: 3, 5, 1, 8 (8 moves to the end)
Pass 2: 3, 1, 5, 8
Pass 3: 1, 3, 5, 8
Pass 4: no swaps are made, so the swap flag stays FALSE and the algorithm stops because the list is sorted.
questions.tip: After each pass the largest unsorted value has 'bubbled' to its correct place.

questions.q:
This algorithm should search the array Names[1:50] for a name and output its position. It contains three errors.
01 Found ← TRUE
02 INPUT Target
03 FOR Index ← 0 TO 50
04    IF Names[Index] = Target
05       THEN
06          Found ← TRUE
07          Position ← Index
08    ENDIF
09 NEXT Index
10 IF Found = TRUE
11    THEN
12       OUTPUT "Found at ", Index
13    ELSE
14       OUTPUT "Not found"
15 ENDIF
Identify two of the errors by line number and write the corrected line for each.
ms: max 4: any two errors, 1 mark for identifying the line and 1 for the correction
questions.model:
Line 01 is wrong because Found starts as TRUE, so 'Found at' would be output even if the name is not there. Correct line: Found ← FALSE
Line 12 outputs the loop counter instead of the stored position. Correct line: OUTPUT "Found at ", Position
(Line 03 is also wrong: the array starts at 1, so it should be FOR Index ← 1 TO 50.)
questions.tip: Check the initial values and the array bounds first – they are the most common planted errors.

questions.q:
The array Scores[1:100] stores 100 integers.
Write an algorithm in pseudocode that:
• inputs a value to search for
• uses a linear search that stops as soon as the value is found
• outputs the position of the value, or "Not found".
ms: conditional loop, e.g. WHILE Found = FALSE AND Index <= 100 (1)
compares Scores[Index] with the search value; sets Found ← TRUE when equal (1)
after the loop outputs the position if found, otherwise "Not found" (1)
questions.model:
INPUT SearchValue
Found ← FALSE
Index ← 1
WHILE Found = FALSE AND Index <= 100 DO
   IF Scores[Index] = SearchValue
      THEN
         Found ← TRUE
      ELSE
         Index ← Index + 1
   ENDIF
ENDWHILE
IF Found = TRUE
   THEN
      OUTPUT "Found at position ", Index
   ELSE
      OUTPUT "Not found"
ENDIF
questions.tip: A FOR loop cannot stop early – use WHILE or REPEAT…UNTIL when asked to stop as soon as it is found.

questions.q:
A website registration form asks for an email address, a password and a date of birth.
(a) Describe three different validation checks, one for each field, stating how each check would be applied. [6]
(b) Describe one verification method that could be used for the password, and explain why verification is needed as well as validation. [2]
ms: (a) email: presence check (1) – the field cannot be left blank (1)
(a) email: format check (1) – must contain one @ and a full stop after it (1)
(a) password: length check (1) – at least 8 characters (1)
(a) date of birth: range check (1) – e.g. between 1900 and today / user at least 13 years old (1)
(a) date of birth: type / format check (1) – must be a valid date DD/MM/YYYY (1)
(a) max 2 marks per field; 1 mark for naming a check, 1 for applying it to that field
(b) double entry: password typed twice and compared; if different, re-enter (1)
(b) validation only checks data is reasonable / follows rules, not that it is what the user intended / correct (1)
questions.model:
(a) Email address: a format check that the entry contains an @ symbol followed later by a full stop, otherwise it is rejected.
Password: a length check that the password has at least 8 characters.
Date of birth: a range check that the date is not in the future and makes the user at least 13 years old.
(b) Double entry: the user types the password twice and the two entries are compared; if they do not match, the password must be re-entered. This is needed because validation only checks that the data is reasonable; a password with a typing mistake could pass the length check but would not be the one the user intended.
questions.tip: Each validation mark pair = name of check + how it applies to THAT field.
